title: Identification and Validation of Liver Transplantation-Induced Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers Using a Bioinformatics and Experimental Approach.
authors: Guiting, Yang; Zhang, Shengfeng; Ji, Liu; Lv, Chengmei; Zhao, Chen; Ling, Maoyao; Liao, Xiaoting; Pan, Linghui
one_liner_zh: 该文通过生物信息学和机器学习识别肝移植后急性肺损伤的生物标志物，虽涉及转录因子网络构建，但核心是疾病诊断标志物而非蛋白质-DNA互作机制建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND Acute lung injury (ALI) after liver transplantation (LT) is a critical complication negatively affecting transplant outcomes and patient survival. However, effective biomarkers for early diagnosis remain unidentified. This study aimed to identify hub biomarkers and signaling pathways involved in post-LT ALI through integrated bioinformatics and machine-learning analyses and to validate their diagnostic potential. MATERIAL AND METHODS Differential gene expression analysis identified 27 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Functional enrichment analyses revealed significant involvement in cytokine-mediated signaling, particularly within the NF-kB and TNF pathways. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) evaluated immune infiltration. Machine-learning algorithms identified crucial biomarkers for ALI prediction. Transcription factor-hub gene and competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) networks were constructed. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) analyses validated biomarker expression patterns in relation to ALI. RESULTS Hub biomarkers identified included CXCL3, CD48, and IRAK3. ssGSEA revealed prominent macrophage and neutrophil infiltration associated with ALI. Machine-learning models confirmed CXCL3, CD48, and IRAK3 as reliable predictive biomarkers, which were incorporated into a robust diagnostic nomogram. scRNA-seq analysis showed cell-type-specific expression patterns for CXCL3, CD48, and IRAK3, with heterogeneous associations across datasets. ELISA validated significantly altered protein levels of CXCL3, CD48, and IRAK3 in post-transplant ALI cases compared with controls. CONCLUSIONS CXCL3, CD48, and IRAK3 are novel and promising diagnostic biomarkers for predicting post-LT ALI. These findings provide foundational insights that could support improved diagnosis, prevention strategies, and targeted therapeutic interventions, ultimately enhancing patient outcomes after liver transplantation.
abstract_zh: 背景 肝移植（LT）术后急性肺损伤（ALI）是一种严重并发症，对移植结局和患者生存产生不利影响。然而，用于早期诊断的有效生物标志物仍未明确。本研究旨在通过整合生物信息学和机器学习分析，识别参与肝移植术后ALI的核心生物标志物及信号通路，并验证其诊断潜力。材料与方法 差异基因表达分析识别出27个差异表达基因（DEGs）。功能富集分析显示其显著参与细胞因子介导的信号传导，尤其是NF-kB和TNF通路。单样本基因集富集分析（ssGSEA）评估了免疫浸润情况。机器学习算法识别出用于ALI预测的关键生物标志物。构建了转录因子-核心基因和竞争性内源RNA（ceRNA）网络。单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）和酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）分析验证了与ALI相关的生物标志物表达模式。结果 识别的核心生物标志物包括CXCL3、CD48和IRAK3。ssGSEA显示与ALI相关的显著巨噬细胞和中性粒细胞浸润。机器学习模型确认CXCL3、CD48和IRAK3为可靠的预测性生物标志物，并将其纳入一个稳健的诊断列线图。scRNA-seq分析显示CXCL3、CD48和IRAK3具有细胞类型特异性表达模式，且在不同数据集中存在异质性关联。ELISA验证了与对照组相比，移植后ALI病例中CXCL3、CD48和IRAK3的蛋白水平显著改变。结论 CXCL3、CD48和IRAK3是预测肝移植术后ALI的新型且有前景的诊断生物标志物。这些发现提供了基础性见解，可能有助于改善诊断、预防策略和靶向治疗干预，最终提升肝移植后的患者结局。
